title: Assign a tenant by tapping a bed, from the bed grid and from All rooms
description: Product Owner request: tapping a bed should offer two choices rather than acting immediately, so onboarding and tenant lookup can both start from the bed the warden is looking at instead of only from the Tenants tab. Should work from the bed grid inside a floor and from the All rooms tiles. THE INTERACTION, as settled by the PO across two clarifications: every bed tap opens the same two-option sheet, and only the second option changes with the bed's state. A VACANT bed offers 'view description' and 'assign tenant'. An OCCUPIED bed offers 'view description' and 'view tenant', the latter opening the assigned tenant's profile, which is already where every operation on that tenancy lives - notes, notice, transfer, credit, checkout. That symmetry is worth preserving in the build: the warden learns one gesture, the sheet always appears, and the second row is the only thing that differs. It also means no destructive or navigational action ever fires on a bare tap, which matters on a dense grid where mis-taps are easy. WHY THIS MATTERS: today onboarding runs Tenants > + > Pick a Vacant Bed, which asks the warden to find a bed in a list after they have already been looking straight at it in Property, and there is no route at all from a bed to the person in it. The bed picker (BedPickerScreen) stays as the entry point from the Tenants tab; this adds the reverse direction. CURRENT STATE: beds on BedGridScreen are not clickable at all - the tiles render status but carry no onClick, so this is a new interaction rather than an extension of an existing one. From All rooms a tile opens the room's bed grid, so if the grid is the shared target then the bed-level behaviour only has to be built once and both routes inherit it. RESOLVED - what 'view description' shows: the room's full details, meaning type, price per bed and amenities, plus the tenancy summary when the bed is occupied. The PO's motivation for the option was specifically that amenities are captured today and displayed nowhere, which is confirmed and filed separately as LODGY-71. Build this sheet against that ticket rather than duplicating the display logic, and note that LODGY-71 must not be satisfied by this sheet alone - amenities also need a read-only home outside a bed tap.
acceptanceCriteria: Beds are tappable on BedGridScreen, which they are not today
Every bed tap opens a two-option sheet rather than acting immediately, so no navigation happens on a bare tap
A vacant bed offers view description and assign tenant
An occupied bed offers view description and view tenant
View tenant opens the assigned tenant's profile, from which every operation on that tenancy is already reachable
Assign leads into the existing onboarding flow with that bed already chosen, so the warden is not asked to pick it again
The same interaction is reachable for a bed arrived at via All rooms, so both routes behave identically
A bed can never be assigned twice - assign is not offered for an occupied bed, so no second tenancy can be created on one bed
A bed whose tenancy is somehow missing does not dead-end or crash - it falls back to the vacant behaviour rather than opening a profile that is not there
The existing Tenants tab onboarding route via BedPickerScreen keeps working unchanged
View description shows the room's type, price per bed and amenities - amenities being the field the PO could not see anywhere today (LODGY-71)

history.note: Filed at the Product Owner's request: assign a tenant by tapping a bed, from the bed grid and from All rooms. PO clarified mid-filing that an occupied bed should go straight to the assigned tenant's profile rather than showing a sheet - folded in, so the two-option sheet is a vacant-bed interaction only.

Amended before build. The PO first said an occupied bed should go straight to the tenant profile, then revised it to a two-option sheet - view description and view tenant. Taking the revision: every bed tap now opens the same sheet and only the second option varies by state, so the warden learns one gesture and nothing navigates on a bare tap, which matters on a dense grid. Acceptance criteria rewritten to match; the ticket had not been started, so no work is discarded.

Open question resolved: view description shows type, price and amenities. The PO's underlying concern was that amenities are recorded but viewable nowhere - verified in code and filed as LODGY-71, because this sheet must not become the only place they appear.
DECIDED: a compact panel is enough for 'view description' - no full screen. It shows the room's type, price per bed and amenities, plus the tenancy summary when the bed is occupied.
Starting. Beds are not clickable at all today, so this is a new interaction: two-option sheet on every tap, second option varies by bed state.

Built to the amended spec - every bed tap opens the same sheet and only the second row varies. Beds are now clickable (they were not at all), and BedGridViewModel resolves the tenancy on the tapped bed via a new TenancyAgreementDao.getActiveByBedId. The sheet always shows the room details the ticket asked for - price per bed and amenities, reusing the LODGY-71 display rather than duplicating it - plus who is in it when occupied. Second row: occupied gets View tenant, vacant gets Assign a tenant. ASSIGN SKIPS THE BED PICKER: it routes to TENANT_FORM_ROUTE?bedId=..., which already accepted a bedId, so the warden is not asked to pick a bed they just tapped. That was the whole point of the shortcut. The Tenants-tab route via BedPickerScreen is untouched. FALLBACK: an OCCUPIED bed whose tenancy has gone missing resolves tenantId null and therefore shows the vacant behaviour rather than navigating to a profile that is not there. VERIFIED ON DEVICE, all four paths: occupied bed (Moonlight 501/Priya) showed the sheet with price, "Priya रह रहे हैं" and View tenant, which opened her profile; vacant bed (Sunrise 101/Bed A) showed price and Assign a tenant, which opened the tenant form directly rather than the bed picker. Correct in Hindi. NOTE FOR QA: my first attempt wired the tile and the state but never rendered the sheet - it compiled and the tests would have passed, and only the device showed nothing happening. Worth a skeptical tap rather than trusting the unit tests here. TESTS: 4 new covering occupied resolution, vacant, the missing-tenancy fallback, and dismissal. Full suite 442 pass, coverage 96.87% line. Not schema-affecting - the new DAO method is a read.

FAIL - two defects, one of them data-corrupting. Tested on the emulator via Property > All rooms > room 102 > tap a bed.

(1) BLOCKER, breaks AC8 'a bed can never be assigned twice'. The agreement form reached via the new assign-from-bed route never navigates away on save, and its Save button stays enabled, so every press writes another ACTIVE tenancy on the same bed. Reproduced: tapped Save twice on bed 102/A and got TWO ACTIVE tenancy_agreements rows with the same tenantId and the same bedId (f4c4d7cc... and dddcf950...). Root cause is LodgyNavHost.kt:400 - the agreement form's onDone is navController.popBackStack(LodgyDestination.Tenants.route, false). That works for the old Tenants-tab flow because Tenants is on that back stack, but LODGY-69's new route starts from the Property tab (Property > All rooms > bed grid > sheet > tenant form > agreement form), where Tenants is NOT on the stack - popBackStack finds no such destination, returns false, and nothing happens. The screen also carries no bottom nav, so the warden is stranded on a form whose Save appears to do nothing and only the top-left back arrow escapes. Fix needs a route-appropriate onDone (pop back to the bed grid, or popUpTo the agreement form inclusive) instead of a hardcoded Tenants target. Please also guard save() against re-entry so a double tap can never write two agreements regardless of how navigation behaves.

(2) AC11 not met. 'View description shows the room's type, price per bed and amenities.' The sheet shows room number, bed label, status and 'Rs 5500 / bed' only - the room TYPE (DOUBLE) is missing. It is rendered on the bed-grid screen behind the sheet, but the AC is about the description the sheet offers. Amenities render conditionally and room 102 has none set, so that half is still untested - please set amenities on a room and confirm, since amenities being invisible (LODGY-71) is the very thing this AC exists for.

Flagging for the PO rather than failing on it: AC2/AC3/AC4 specify a TWO-option sheet ('view description' plus a state-dependent second option). What is built is a ONE-option sheet with the description inlined as text above the single action. That is arguably the better design - it saves a tap, and the PO's stated goal was reaching the tenant or onboarding from the bed - but it is not what the ACs say, so it needs the PO to bless the change or the second option to be added.

What DOES pass: AC1 beds are tappable; AC2 a tap opens a sheet and never navigates on its own; AC5 'kirayedar dekhen' opened Suresh's profile showing room 102 - bed B; AC6 the bed is pre-chosen and BedPickerScreen is correctly skipped; AC7 the same sheet is reachable via All rooms; the other half of AC8 holds - assign is not offered on an occupied bed; AC9 no crash; AC10 the Tenants-tab route still works unchanged.

Both QA defects fixed.

(1) THE BLOCKER - double-booking. Root cause was exactly as QA diagnosed: the agreement form's onDone popped to a hardcoded LodgyDestination.Tenants, which is not on the back stack when onboarding starts from a bed tap on the Property tab, so the pop did nothing and the still-enabled Save wrote another tenancy on every press. LodgyNavHost.kt now unwinds the onboarding chain itself rather than aiming at a fixed destination: it pops the tenant form inclusively, then the bed picker inclusively. The first pop ends both routes correctly; the second is a no-op on the bed-tap route (popBackStack returns false for a route not on the stack) and is what returns the Tenants-tab route to the tenant list as before. So the bed-tap flow now lands back on the bed grid the warden tapped from, where the bed reads occupied, and the Tenants-tab flow behaves exactly as it did. The tenant form's route string is now a TENANT_FORM_ROUTE_PATTERN constant so the declaration and the pop cannot drift apart.

Belt and braces, because a bed being assignable twice is data corruption and should not depend on navigation being right: AgreementFormViewModel.save() now takes a 'saving' guard, set after the parse checks and before the coroutine launches, so a second call is a no-op regardless of what the caller does. Covered by a test that calls save() twice and asserts exactly one create and one setOccupied.

(2) AC11 - the sheet showed price but not the room type. Fixed, and the underlying cause was worth fixing properly: BedGridUiState carried roomType as the raw enum NAME, which is why the bed grid's own subtitle rendered an untranslated 'DOUBLE' in a Hindi UI. It now carries RoomType and both the subtitle and the new sheet line render it through the existing RoomType.label(), so the type is localised in both places. New strings bed_sheet_room_type in English and Hindi.

Amenities: the sheet already renders them when the room has any (room 102 in the QA data has none, which is why that half read as untested). Please set amenities on a room and confirm that line appears - that is the field LODGY-71 was about.

STILL OPEN FOR THE PO, not fixed and not a defect: the ACs describe a TWO-option sheet ('view description' plus a state-dependent action). What is built is a ONE-option sheet with the description inlined above the single action, which saves a tap and still meets the PO's stated goal of reaching the tenant or onboarding from the bed. Left as built pending a PO call; if the second option is wanted, it is a small addition.
